transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... I just keep getting hit out of nowhere with this one specific memory. It's the scene of my cousin on the pavement. It's like, suddenly I can hear the shouting and see all the lights flashing again. And it happens even when I'm just standing in the church office, trying to do my job and act normal. It's just really severe, and I don't know how to stop it.
How long have you been experiencing these sudden memories and flashbacks?
This has been going on for a while now. It started right after my cousin was killed, which was... two years and three months ago.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of your cousin's death?

Yeah, I do. I actually take the long way around town now, just so I don't have to pass the community center or that court. And if somebody brings it up... if they start talking about that night, I just shut it down. Or I'll just find a reason to leave the room. I just can't deal with it.
Do you often feel negative emotions like fear, anger, or guilt connected to what happened to your cousin?

Yeah, I do. Honestly, most days I just feel this heavy mix of fear, anger, and guilt sitting right in my chest from the minute I wake up. It's just... always there. I feel like I failed God, and my family, and... and the kids who trusted me. It's just a constant weight.
Do you find it hard to experience positive emotions, like happiness or love, even when you’re around people you care about?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... I still feel love for my family and the people in my church. I can still laugh and feel happy when I'm around them. It's just that those other heavy feelings are usually hanging over me at the same time. But no, I haven't lost the ability to feel the good things.
Do you often feel on edge, easily startled, or have trouble sleeping since the incident?

Yeah, definitely. I'm just... I'm always on edge now. Like, if I'm at a restaurant or a meeting, I can't sit with my back to a door anymore. I just can't do it. And even at church events, where I should be focused, I'm just... I'm always watching people's hands, checking the corners of the room, watching cars slow down outside. I'm always looking for the nearest exit instead of actually paying attention to the people right in front of me.

Have you noticed that these flashbacks and intrusive memories happen more often in response to specific triggers, like sounds or sights that remind you of what happened, or do they seem to come up without any clear reason?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't noticed if it's specific things setting it off or if it just happens on its own. It's just... it just happens. I haven't really been able to track a clear pattern or anything like that.

Have you found yourself believing negative things about yourself, other people, or the world in general since your cousin’s death—like thinking you’re bad, that people can’t be trusted, or that the world is dangerous?

No, I wouldn't say I feel that way. I mean, obviously, losing my cousin was terrible, and the way it happened was awful, but... I don't think I'm bad, or that everyone is out to get me. My faith teaches me a lot about trust and the good in people, and I still believe that. I know the world has danger in it, but I don't walk around thinking everything is completely ruined or that people are inherently untrustworthy. It's more just the physical feeling of being on edge that I mentioned before, rather than my actual beliefs changing.
Have you found yourself thinking that you’re to blame for what happened, or that you’re a failure, especially when you reflect on your cousin’s death?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I think about it a lot. I just keep telling myself that if I had... if I had just ended the event earlier, or if I had walked him out myself, you know? Or if I had just kept a better watch over those boys... my cousin would still be here. It's hard not to feel like it's my fault.
